question.text:
You are evaluating the performance of two commodity ETFs over the past quarter: ETF X (Gold): Total Return = 5%, Expense Ratio = 0.5% ETF Y (Oil): Total Return = 7%, Expense Ratio = 0.75%
Compute the gross return for ETF Y before expenses.

explanation.text: The Logic: Gross return is the total return before deducting expenses. For ETF Y, total return is stated as 7%, so gross return = 7%. The Trap: Option 6.25% tempts candidates who subtract the expense ratio (7% - 0.75%) thinking 'net' is being asked; 5% and 5.25% are noise from misreading the X vs Y data. The trap is not reading the word 'gross' carefully. Cross-Exam Context: Gross-vs-net return distinction is tested in NISM-V-A (Mutual Fund Distributors), NISM-V-B (Mutual Fund Foundation), and NISM-XXI-A (PMS Distributors). Distributor's Pro-Tip: When a factsheet quotes 'total return', assume it is pre-fees unless the line item says 'net of expenses' - for client reporting, PMS distributors must always re-compute and disclose the net-of-all-fees number, per SEBI mandatory-disclosure format.
